## Biological Narrative

The RaMP enrichment analysis identifies **Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG map00260)** as the top affected pathway, with a remarkable fold-enrichment of 568.9 (FDR = 0.0) across six matched input metabolites: ornithine (C00077), 2-ketobutyric acid (C00109), lipoic acid (C16241), S-adenosylhomocysteine (C00021), L-cysteine (C00097), and L-methionine (C00073). A second strongly supported candidate is **Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives (Reactome R-HSA-71291)**, which shares most of the same drivers and reflects broader amino-group metabolism disruption.

The enrichment pattern converges on the **methionine cycle** as a central hub. L-methionine (C00073) is confirmed upstream of S-adenosylhomocysteine (C00021) via S-adenosylmethionine (C00019) in just two KEGG reaction steps, establishing a clear directional relationship. L-cysteine (C00097) connects to S-adenosylhomocysteine through a longer four-hop path, implicating the transsulfuration pathway that links one-carbon metabolism to glutathione precursor supply. Ornithine (C00077) participates in arginine and proline metabolism, which cross-talks with the methionine cycle, while 2-ketobutyric acid (C00109) feeds the serine-threonine axis from the glycolytic side.

In biological terms, coordinated elevation of these six metabolites points to **widespread disruption of one-carbon and amino-group metabolism**. S-adenosylhomocysteine is a direct by-product of methyltransferase reactions; elevated levels can inhibit S-adenosylmethionine–dependent methyltransferases, broadly suppressing methylation capacity. Lipoic acid (C16241) participates as an essential cofactor in the oxidative decarboxylation that links the methionine cycle to the citric acid cycle. Phenylephrine (C07441), while not driving these pathways directly, may reflect an independent adrenergic perturbation or be metabolized through overlapping pathways. Nitrate (C00244) and 5,6-dihydroxyindole (C05578) suggest parallel shifts in nitrogen balance and melanogenic or oxidative stress axes.

Collectively, the data are most consistent with **altered methyl-group availability and amino-acid flux** in the treatment group, with L-methionine and S-adenosylhomocysteine serving as the primary drivers of the metabolic disturbance.

L-cysteine (C00097) connects to S-adenosylhomocysteine through a longer path. Ornithine (C00077) and 2-ketobutyric acid (C00109) are matched members of the glycine, serine and threonine metabolism pathway alongside the methionine-cycle intermediates.

In biological terms, the coordinated elevation of these six metabolites is consistent with perturbation of **Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG map00260)** and its associated amino-acid network. S-adenosylhomocysteine is a direct by-product of methyltransferase reactions; elevated levels can inhibit S-adenosylmethionine–dependent methyltransferases, broadly suppressing methylation capacity. Lipoic acid (C16241) participates as an essential cofactor in oxidative decarboxylation reactions within this metabolic zone. **Limitations:** Three input metabolites (1-pyrroline-5-carboxylic acid, 5,6-dihydroxyindole, phenylephrine) did not map to the enriched pathway and were not further connected in this analysis, limiting the completeness of the biological picture for these compounds.
